title: Repair Drywall After Removing Wallpaper: Step-by-Step
h1: How to Repair Drywall After Removing Wallpaper: Seal, Skim Coat and Prime
description: Repair drywall after removing wallpaper the right way: clean off paste, seal torn paper with oil or shellac primer, skim coat and prime for a smooth wall.
secondary_keywords: how to fix torn drywall paper
excerpt: Torn drywall paper after stripping wallpaper? Clean off paste, seal with the right primer, skim coat and prime so paint goes on smooth with no bubbles.
image_alt: Wall being repaired after wallpaper removal with joint compound spread over sealed drywall using a wide taping knife
key_takeaways: Wash off all wallpaper paste first; leftover residue makes paint crack.
Cut away loose drywall paper with a sharp utility knife until only firmly attached paper remains.
Seal torn brown paper with oil-based or shellac-based primer, or a gypsum sealer, before any joint compound, or it will bubble.
Skim coat the whole wall if damage is widespread, then sand with 120–150 grit.
Prime new compound with PVA or high-build primer before painting to prevent flashing.

faq.q: How do you fix torn drywall paper after removing wallpaper?
faq.a: Cut away any loose or lifting paper with a sharp utility knife, lightly sand fuzzy fibers, then seal the exposed brown paper with an oil-based or shellac-based primer or a gypsum sealer. Once it is dry, cover the area with thin coats of joint compound, sand smooth and prime with a drywall primer before painting.

faq.q: Why does joint compound bubble on torn drywall?
faq.a: Joint compound is water-based. When it touches exposed brown drywall paper, the paper absorbs the water, swells and lifts away from the gypsum, creating bubbles. Sealing the torn paper first with a solvent-based or shellac-based primer, or a penetrating gypsum sealer, keeps water out so the compound bonds to a stable surface.

faq.q: Can I paint directly over drywall after removing wallpaper?
faq.a: Only if the face paper is intact and every trace of adhesive has been washed off. Even then, prime first. Paint applied over leftover paste can crack or wrinkle, and paint over torn paper or fresh compound will look patchy. Use oil or shellac primer over residue or torn paper and drywall primer over new compound.

faq.q: Do I need to skim coat after removing wallpaper?
faq.a: You need a skim coat when torn paper or patches cover a large part of the wall, roughly a quarter or more, or when side lighting would show uneven areas. A skim coat gives a uniform surface so paint looks even. For a few small tears or gouges, sealing and spot repairs are usually enough.

faq.q: What primer should I use on damaged drywall?
faq.a: Use an oil-based or shellac-based primer, or a dedicated gypsum sealer, on exposed brown paper and on areas with possible adhesive residue. After filling and skim coating, use a PVA or high-build drywall primer over the new joint compound before painting. Avoid latex or PVA primer directly on torn paper.
